note: Independent vectors for detached, exact-octet artifact identity (issue #25).
Deliberately separate from tests/fixtures/conformance/, which is the closed
semantic canonicalization conformance manifest. Nothing here canonicalizes,
validates, or reinterprets anything: an artifact_id is SHA-256 over
<domain> || 0x00 || <the exact artifact bytes>, and equal IDs claim only
equal kind and equal octets. contract_id and interface_id are semantic
Contract identities and source_bundle_id is a raw-source bundle content
identity; an artifact ID is none of those. See docs/artifact-identity-v1.md.

vectors.name: empty
vectors.note: Framing anchor: no artifact bytes at all, so the domain tag and the single 0x00 separator are the whole preimage. Also shows that an artifact_id exists for bytes that are not a valid artifact — computing one is not a validity claim.

vectors.name: contract
vectors.note: Baseline raw Contract document: the same Contract the envelope and compilation vectors carry, serialized on its own with no enclosing envelope and no provenance sidecar.

vectors.name: contract_producer
vectors.note: Only producer.name and producer.version were rewritten. Raw Contract bytes contain producer, so the Contract artifact ID moves; contract_id and interface_id exclude producer and are byte-identical, which is exactly why a semantic identity cannot stand in for an artifact identity.

vectors.name: contract_envelope
vectors.note: Baseline envelope: a strict Contract plus one namespaced extension.

vectors.name: contract_envelope_extension_name
vectors.note: Only the extension name changed. contract_id is unchanged because extensions are outside it; artifact_id changes because the octets changed.

vectors.name: contract_envelope_extension_value
vectors.note: Only one extension value changed, including the package_version-carrying object. Package metadata is covered exactly when it is present in the supplied artifact bytes, and never by contract_id.

vectors.name: contract_envelope_compact
vectors.note: The identical JSON value rendered by a different encoder: same meaning, no whitespace, different octets, different artifact_id. This is the exact-octet claim, stated as a vector.

vectors.name: compilation
vectors.note: Baseline compilation: the same Contract plus its SourceInfo provenance sidecar.

vectors.name: compilation_source_doc
vectors.note: One doc comment changed in the entry source. A doc comment is not semantic, so contract_id is unchanged while source_bundle_id, the sidecar, and artifact_id all move.

vectors.name: compilation_producer
vectors.note: Only producer.name and producer.version were rewritten. The document still validates and still carries the identical contract_id, which is precisely why contract_id must not be treated as an artifact or provenance identity.

shared_contract_id.note: Every member embeds this identical semantic contract_id and every member has a distinct artifact_id. That difference is the whole point of issue #25.
